feature_name: Runtime contracts split from engine (dependency-direction gate)
feature_description: Split ResearchRunRequest, ResearchRunResult, and RunConflictError out of runtime/engine.py into a new runtime/contracts.py, and repoint the four modules that only ever needed the contracts (cli.py, runtime/batch.py, product/research.py, backtest/validation.py) so they stop transitively depending on ResearchEngine's SQLite storage (storage.recovery, storage.sqlite).
entrypoint: uv run pytest tests/unit/test_import_layering.py -k 'runtime_contracts or contract_only';uv run pytest tests/unit/runtime/test_contracts_import_isolation.py
acceptance_test: tests/unit/runtime/test_contracts_import_isolation.py::test_importing_runtime_contracts_in_a_fresh_process_does_not_load_the_storage_layer
notes: Also exercised by test_runtime_contracts_module_does_not_import_runtime_engine, test_runtime_contracts_module_does_not_transitively_depend_on_storage, and test_contract_only_consumers_do_not_transitively_reach_engine_owned_storage_modules in tests/unit/test_import_layering.py, all using grimp.build_graph per the existing Task-4 idiom, not runtime sys.modules introspection. Verified by mutation: reverting any one of the four modules' import line back to `from openalpha_cn.runtime.engine import ...` makes the direct-edge test fail. The transitive-storage check is scoped to storage.recovery/storage.sqlite specifically, not all of openalpha_cn.storage, because two of the four modules retain real, pre-existing, unrelated storage touchpoints out of this task's scope: cli.py separately needs backtest.replay.ReplayCorpus (which needs the full ResearchEngine for its `replay` subcommand), and runtime.batch has its own TYPE_CHECKING-only reference to storage.batch.SQLiteBatchTaskStore for an unrelated method parameter. runtime/__init__.py resolves ResearchEngine lazily via a module __getattr__ (PEP 562) instead of an eager top-level import, because Python always executes a package's __init__.py before any of its submodules -- an eager import there would silently reintroduce the storage dependency at real runtime for anyone merely importing runtime.contracts. A reviewer proved that guard previously had no automated backstop: grimp records function-local and eager top-level imports as the same static edge, so it cannot see whether ResearchEngine resolution actually runs at import time. That gap is now closed by tests/unit/runtime/test_contracts_import_isolation.py::test_importing_runtime_contracts_in_a_fresh_process_does_not_load_the_storage_layer, a subprocess-isolated test (launched via sys.executable, so it runs under the same interpreter/venv as the rest of the suite) that imports openalpha_cn.runtime.contracts in a brand-new Python process and asserts openalpha_cn.storage and every submodule under it are absent from that process's real sys.modules -- an in-process check would be meaningless, since pytest has already imported most of openalpha_cn, including the storage layer, by the time any test runs. Verified by mutation: temporarily making runtime/__init__.py's ResearchEngine import eager makes this test fail, naming the leaked openalpha_cn.storage, .memory, .parquet, .recovery, and .sqlite modules; restoring the lazy form makes it pass again. This is a narrow, deliberate exception to the task brief's general prohibition on runtime sys.modules checks: that prohibition targets the dependency-direction assertions above, where grimp's static analysis is the right tool; here static analysis is structurally blind to eager-vs-lazy import timing, so a runtime check is the only tool that can verify this specific property. The test deliberately does not assert bare sqlite3 absence from sys.modules: models/governance.py imports sqlite3 directly at module scope for ModelRegistry's durable usage accounting, reached from runtime.contracts via agents.base -> agents/__init__.py -> agents.model -> models.base -> models/__init__.py -> models.openai_compatible -> models.governance, a separate, already-tracked layering exemption (baseline entry V2-P0B-011, models.governance -> sqlite3) unrelated to ResearchEngine's lazy resolution and out of this task's scope; asserting bare sqlite3 absence would fail permanently regardless of whether the guard under test is eager or lazy, so it would not discriminate the regression this test exists to catch.

feature_description: Define typing.Protocol interfaces (RunRepository, RecoveryStore, BatchTaskStore, PortfolioLedger, EvidenceStore, WatchlistStore, ReportStore) for 7 of the 9 concrete storage classes ADR-0001 claimed had an abstraction but did not; retype ResearchEngine.__init__ (repository, recovery_store), BatchResearchService.__init__ (store), and PortfolioBacktestRunner.__init__ (ledger) against them, and make ResearchEngine.recovery_store a required caller-injected parameter instead of self-constructing SQLiteRecoveryStore(repository.path) from repository.path. Each Protocol declares only the methods its actual consumer(s) call, not the concrete class's full public surface.

Structural conformance is mypy-enforced, not merely conventional: temporarily narrowing SQLiteRunRepository.get_run's parameter from str to int makes `uv run mypy src scripts` reject all four Protocol-typed call sites (backtest/replay.py:121, sdk.py:109, api/app.py:267, api/app.py:349) with 'incompatible type ... expected RunRepository', reverted after confirming. engine.py's self-constructed SQLiteRecoveryStore(repository.path) is removed; recovery_store is now a required parameter injected by sdk.py, api/app.py (twice), and backtest/replay.py (which now also constructs one). test_legal_downward_imports_from_runtime_and_backtest_into_storage_are_not_flagged in test_import_layering.py was updated (2 of its 4 direct-import assertions flip from True to False) because it pinned runtime.engine->storage.sqlite and backtest.multi_day->storage.portfolio as legitimate direct imports, both of which this task's Protocol retyping deliberately removes; the other two assertions (runtime.engine->storage.recovery, backtest.replay->storage.sqlite) are unchanged, and backtest.replay->storage.recovery is newly added. Verified by mutation, one concrete class at a time, each reverted after confirming: narrowing ParquetEvidenceStore.append's items parameter from `tuple[EvidenceSnapshot, ...]` to `int` makes mypy reject sdk.py:66 and api/app.py:258 with 'Incompatible types in assignment ... expected EvidenceStore'; narrowing SQLiteWatchlistStore.put's entry parameter from `WatchlistEntry` to `int` makes mypy reject sdk.py:72 and api/app.py:264 the same way against WatchlistStore; narrowing SQLiteReportStore.append's report parameter from `ResearchReport` to `int` makes mypy reject sdk.py:73 and api/app.py:265 against ReportStore. All seven storage Protocols defined in this task are now wired into at least one mypy-checked consumer signature; none remain decorative.
